title: Quantified acceptance for latency tail behaviors and controlled traffic-shifts for model promotions
creator: Ava Nguyen
description: Problem: We lack a precise, testable acceptance definition for how tail latency behaves during model promotions and tenant traffic shifts. Without quantified acceptance criteria we regress customer experience when promoting new model variants (quantized, batched, or kernel-optimized) and risk repeated rollbacks. Scope: Define measurable acceptance gates (latency bands, availability floors, error budget burn rules) and a deterministic traffic-shift algorithm for canaries/rollouts across multi-tenant traffic. Exclude: billing/quotas tuning and infra capacity procurement (separate initiatives).
acceptance_criteria: Define numeric latency envelopes for interactive endpoints: p50/p95/p99 for short-chat (<=256 tokens) and long-chat (>256 tokens) categories
Specify availability target and error-rate ceiling during promotions: 99.8% successful-response rate per minute for promoted traffic, and 99.95% for steady-state global service
Establish error-budget burn thresholds that trigger automatic halt and rollback: 3x expected burn-rate over a 30-minute window OR >5% absolute increase in per-tenant 5-min error-rate
Traffic-shift algorithm: step increments capped at 5% of total traffic every 10 minutes with health-check gates evaluated at p95 latency and 1-minute success-rate
Canary allocation rules: prefer small sample of low-affinity tenants and synthetic traffic (reserve 10% of canary traffic for high-priority customers with opt-in)
Define monitoring dashboard queries and alert conditions: p99 increase >30ms over baseline for 5 consecutive minutes; canary burn-rate exceed threshold => active rollback
Document post-promotion validation checklist (production eval run, regression prompts, embedding drift check) and required artifacts for sign-off
decisions: Use dual baselining: historical 28-day median + last-7-day rolling baseline to avoid stale baselines when load patterns shift
Promoted variant must implement the same KV cache key semantics as the baseline; if not, it requires manual approval and stricter canary gates
Allow quantized model variants for promotion only if p99 tail latency increase is <= 10% and cost-per-token improvement >= 15% in controlled benchmarks
Automate rollback on diagnostic signal: if error-budget burn triggers AND p99 tail increases by >25ms in the canary cohort -> immediate traffic-shift reversal to previous stable variant
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Drafted ticket and initial problem statement; synced with Eng infra lead (Kai) and SRE (Marisol) to confirm metric availability
2026-03-11: Product/Eng workshop — agreed on 5% step size and 10-minute evaluation window. Eng requested a decision on using last-7-day vs last-28-day baseline (dual baseline chosen)

2026-03-12: Created prototype dashboard queries and synthetic canary harness in staging (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2987). Waiting on ENG-90114 to expose per-tenant burn-rate metric in metrics pipeline
Planned next: finalize acceptance wording, add automated runbook entries, and prepare a short PRD excerpt for executive review by 2026-03-16
notes: Trade-offs considered: smaller step sizes reduce user blast radius but lengthen rollout time; 5%/10min chosen as pragmatic middle ground after benchmarking rollout times on bursty workloads
Per-tenant isolation: for tenants with strict SLAs we will require explicit opt-in to promotions; default behavior is conservative for high-value tenants
Rollout cadence: we avoid global promotions during known peak windows (per region) — scheduling guidance to be added to Console release flow
